operations.specification: Implementation: 1) Validate email format (must contain @ and valid domain structure). 2) Check email uniqueness by querying todo_app_users table where email = request.email (case-insensitive comparison). 3) Validate password against complexity requirements: minimum 8 characters, maximum 128 characters, at least one uppercase letter (A-Z), one lowercase letter (a-z), one digit (0-9), one special character from !@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{};'\":,./<>?. 4) If any validation fails, return appropriate error code (INVALID_EMAIL_FORMAT, EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED, or WEAK_PASSWORD with specific unmet requirements). 5) Hash password using bcrypt with cost factor 12 or higher. 6) Create user record in todo_app_users with: id (UUID), email (lowercased), password_hash, display_name (initialize to email), failed_attempt_count (0), locked_until (null), created_at/updated_at (current timestamp), deleted_at (null). 7) Create session record in todo_app_user_sessions with: id (UUID), todo_app_user_id, ip (from request context), href (request URL), referrer (from headers), created_at (current timestamp), expired_at (current + refresh token lifetime). 8) Generate JWT access token (15 min expiration) with claims: sub (user id), iat, exp, role ('user'), jti (unique token id). 9) Generate JWT refresh token (30 days expiration) with claims: sub, iat, exp, type ('refresh'), jti. 10) Return response with both tokens and user identifier. Must complete within 3 seconds under normal conditions.
operations.description:
Registers a new user account in the TodoApp private multi-user Todo application.

This endpoint creates a new user account with the provided email and password credentials. The system validates email format and uniqueness, enforces password strength requirements, and securely hashes the password before storage. Upon successful registration, the user receives JWT access and refresh tokens for immediate authentication.

The email address serves as the unique identifier for authentication and must not already exist in the system. The password must meet complexity requirements: 8-128 characters with at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one digit, and one special character. The display_name field is automatically initialized to the email address upon registration.

Security considerations include bcrypt password hashing with cost factor 12+, timing-safe operations to prevent enumeration attacks, and rate limiting (5 requests per minute per IP). The system never stores passwords in plaintext and returns the same error code for duplicate emails to prevent email enumeration.

Upon successful registration, the user is immediately authenticated with a new session record created in todo_app_user_sessions, capturing IP address and request metadata for audit purposes. The returned tokens allow immediate access to protected endpoints.

requestBody.description: Registration credentials including email and password with confirmation.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and user identifier for the newly registered user.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Implementation: 1) Validate request body contains both email and password fields. 2) Find user in todo_app_users table by email (case-insensitive query). 3) If user not found, return INVALID_CREDENTIALS error (do not reveal email doesn't exist). 4) Check locked_until field: if set and current time < locked_until, return ACCOUNT_LOCKED error with remaining lock duration. 5) Verify password hash using bcrypt.compare() with timing-safe comparison. 6) If password invalid: increment failed_attempt_count. If count reaches 5, set locked_until to current time + 15 minutes. Return INVALID_CREDENTIALS error. 7) If password valid: reset failed_attempt_count to 0, set locked_until to null. 8) Update user record with new failed_attempt_count and locked_until values. 9) Create session record in todo_app_user_sessions with: id (UUID), todo_app_user_id, ip (from request context), href (request URL), referrer (from headers), created_at (current timestamp), expired_at (current + refresh token lifetime). 10) Generate JWT access token (15 min expiration) with claims: sub (user id), iat, exp, role ('user'), jti. 11) Generate JWT refresh token (30 days expiration) with claims: sub, iat, exp, type ('refresh'), jti. 12) Return response with both tokens and user identifier. Must complete within 2 seconds under normal conditions. Never include password or password_hash in any response.
operations.description:
Authenticates a user with email and password credentials in the TodoApp private multi-user Todo application.

This endpoint validates user credentials and issues JWT tokens for authenticated access. The system implements account lockout protection after 5 consecutive failed login attempts, with a 15-minute lockout period to prevent brute force attacks.

The authentication process uses timing-safe comparison to prevent timing attacks and returns a generic INVALID_CREDENTIALS error for both non-existent emails and incorrect passwords, preventing email enumeration. The email field in todo_app_users table has a unique constraint ensuring single account per email.

Account security features include: failed_attempt_count tracking in todo_app_users, automatic account lockout via locked_until timestamp, and lockout reset upon successful authentication. The system records each login session in todo_app_user_sessions with connection metadata (IP address, request URL, referrer header) for audit trails.

Rate limiting is enforced at 10 requests per minute per IP address. Successful authentication returns both an access token (15-minute expiration) for API calls and a refresh token (30-day expiration) for session persistence. Users can maintain multiple active sessions across different devices.

requestBody.description: Login credentials containing email address and password.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and user identifier for the authenticated user.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Implementation: 1) Extract refresh token from request body. 2) Verify JWT signature using the configured secret key (HS256 or RS256 algorithm). 3) Decode token and validate claims: exp (not expired), type (must be 'refresh'), jti (token identifier). 4) Check if token has been revoked by querying a token blacklist (if implemented) or validating against todo_app_user_sessions where id = jti and session is still valid (expired_at > current time). 5) If token is invalid, revoked, or expired, return TOKEN_REVOKED or TOKEN_EXPIRED error requiring re-authentication. 6) Extract user id from token's sub claim. 7) Verify user still exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null) by querying todo_app_users. 8) Optionally rotate refresh token: invalidate old token (add jti to blacklist or mark session expired) and generate new refresh token. 9) Generate new JWT access token (15 min expiration) with claims: sub (user id), iat, exp, role ('user'), jti (new unique token id). 10) If rotating, generate new refresh token (30 days expiration) with claims: sub, iat, exp, type ('refresh'), jti (new unique id). 11) Return response with new access token and optionally new refresh token. Must complete within 1 second under normal conditions.
operations.description:
Renews authentication tokens using a valid refresh token in the TodoApp private multi-user Todo application.

This endpoint allows clients to obtain a new access token when the current one expires, without requiring the user to re-enter credentials. The refresh token must be valid (not expired, not revoked) and associated with an active user account.

The refresh token is a JWT with a 30-day expiration time, containing claims: sub (user id), iat (issued at), exp (expiration), type ('refresh'), and jti (unique token identifier). Token validation includes signature verification, expiration checking, and revocation status.

Security measures include optional refresh token rotation for enhanced security - issuing a new refresh token and invalidating the old one prevents token reuse attacks. The system validates that the user account associated with the refresh token is still active (deleted_at is null in todo_app_users) before issuing new tokens.

Rate limiting is enforced at 20 requests per minute per IP address. If the refresh token is invalid, expired, or revoked, the client must re-authenticate via the login endpoint. The new access token has a 15-minute expiration and enables continued access to protected endpoints.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for renewing authentication session.

responseBody.description: New authentication tokens and user identifier.

operations.name: refresh

operations.description:
Update the authenticated user's profile display name.

This operation allows authenticated users to update their display name, which serves as their chosen identifier within the application. The display name is used for personalization and can be changed any number of times without restrictions.

The display name must be between 1 and 50 characters in length and cannot consist solely of whitespace characters. Unlike the email address which is used for authentication, the display name can be customized to reflect the user's preferred identity and does not need to be unique across the system.

This operation is subject to complete privacy enforcement - users can only update their own profile, and no mechanism exists to modify other users' profiles.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:
1. Extract authenticated user ID from JWT token in request headers
2. Validate request body: display_name must be 1-50 chars, not blank
3. Query todo_app_users table to find user by ID
4. Verify user exists and is not deleted (deleted_at is null)
5. Update display_name field in todo_app_users table
6. Update updated_at timestamp to current time
7. Return updated profile with display_name

Validation rules:
- display_name minLength: 1 character
- display_name maxLength: 50 characters
- display_name must not be blank (not just whitespace)

Error handling:
- Return 401 if not authenticated
- Return 400 if validation fails with specific error codes:
  - PROFILE_DISPLAY_NAME_TOO_SHORT
  - PROFILE_DISPLAY_NAME_TOO_LONG
  - PROFILE_DISPLAY_NAME_BLANK

responseBody.description: Updated user profile with display name

requestBody.description: New display name for the user profile

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of the authenticated user's login sessions.

This operation provides visibility into all active and expired sessions for security awareness and account management purposes. Users can monitor where and when they have authenticated, helping identify suspicious activity or manage sessions across multiple devices.

Each session record includes the IP address from which authentication occurred, the full request URL path, and timestamps for session creation and expiration. This enables users to verify their login history and identify any unauthorized access attempts.

The session list is automatically scoped to the authenticated user, ensuring complete privacy. Users cannot view sessions belonging to other accounts. Sessions are typically ordered by creation date (newest first) to show recent authentication activity.

This endpoint supports the session management workflow where users can review their active logins before deciding to logout from specific devices or change their password to invalidate all sessions.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query todo_app_user_sessions table with automatic user-scoped filtering.

Implementation steps:
1. Extract authenticated user ID from JWT token context
2. Build Prisma query with WHERE clause: todo_app_user_id = current_user_id
3. Apply optional filters from request body:
   - created_at range (from/to)
   - expired_at range (from/to)
   - is_active boolean (expired_at > now() for active sessions)
   - IP address partial match
4. Apply pagination with cursor-based or offset-based approach
5. Order by created_at DESC (newest first) by default
6. Include related user information for display_name if needed
7. Transform results to ISummary format with essential fields only

Response fields:
- id: session identifier
- ip: IP address from authentication
- href: request URL path
- created_at: when session was created
- expired_at: when session expires

No sensitive data (passwords, tokens) should be included in the response.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for session list

operations.description:
Retrieves detailed information about a specific user session for security and audit purposes.

This endpoint allows authenticated users to view their own session details, including the IP address from which the session was created, the request URL that initiated authentication, and the HTTP referrer header. This information helps users monitor their account security and identify potentially unauthorized access.

The session includes creation and expiration timestamps, enabling users to understand session lifetime and validity. Sessions are automatically created during the login process and cannot be manually created or modified by users.

Users can only access sessions that belong to their own account. Attempting to access another user's session will result in a 404 Not Found response to prevent information disclosure about the existence of other users' sessions.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the todo_app_user_sessions table by primary key (id) to retrieve a single session record.

Implementation steps:
1. Extract sessionId from path parameters
2. Validate sessionId is a valid UUID format
3. Query todo_app_user_sessions where id = sessionId
4. Verify the session belongs to the authenticated user (todo_app_user_id matches current user's id)
5. If not found or not owned, return 404 Not Found
6. Return the session entity with all fields

The query should include a join with todo_app_users to verify ownership. The response includes: id, ip, href, referrer (nullable), created_at, and expired_at. Do not include the todo_app_user_id in the response for security reasons.

responseBody.description: Session details including IP address, request metadata, and timestamps

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the session to retrieve
parameters.name: sessionId

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated user's profile information.

This operation returns the current user's display name, which serves as their personalized identifier within the application. The display name is initialized to the user's email address upon registration and can be customized at any time through the profile update operation.

Privacy is strictly enforced: users can only access their own profile through this endpoint. The response contains only the display name field, excluding all internal identifiers, authentication data, and metadata to maintain the privacy-first design principle of this application.

The display name must be between 1 and 50 characters and cannot consist solely of whitespace. Multiple users may have identical display names as uniqueness is not required.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. Extract authenticated user ID from the JWT session token in the Authorization header
2. Query the todo_app_users table to find the user record by ID
3. Verify the user exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL)
4. Return only the display_name field in the response
5. If user not found or session invalid, return 401 Unauthorized error

Database query:
- SELECT display_name FROM todo_app_users WHERE id = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL

Response construction:
- Build ITodoAppUser object containing only display_name
- Do not expose id, email, password_hash, or any other fields

Error handling:
- 401 if not authenticated or session expired
- 401 if user account has been deleted

responseBody.description: User's profile containing the display name

operations.description:
Create a new todo item for the authenticated user.

This operation allows users to create personal todo items with a required title and optional additional details. The title field is mandatory and must not exceed 200 characters. An optional description can be provided up to 5000 characters, preserving all formatting including line breaks and whitespace.

Optional start_date and due_date fields can be specified in ISO 8601 format to indicate when the todo should be started and completed. These dates can include or exclude time components according to user preference.

Upon creation, the todo is automatically associated with the authenticated user ensuring complete privacy isolation. The system generates a unique identifier and sets initial timestamps (created_at and updated_at). The completion status defaults to incomplete (is_completed = false) and the soft delete flag is set to false.

All todo data is strictly scoped to the owning user - no cross-user access is possible. The response includes the complete todo entity with all fields as stored in the database.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. Validate authentication - extract user_id from JWT token in Authorization header
2. Validate request body:
   - title: required, non-empty after trimming, max 200 characters
   - description: optional, max 5000 characters if provided, can be null
   - startDate: optional, valid ISO 8601 date/datetime if provided
   - dueDate: optional, valid ISO 8601 date/datetime if provided
3. Generate UUID for todo id
4. Set defaults:
   - is_completed = false
   - is_deleted = false
   - created_at = current timestamp
   - updated_at = current timestamp
5. Insert into todo_app_todos table with user_id from authenticated session
6. Return complete entity with all fields including generated id and timestamps

Error handling:
- 401 Unauthorized if not authenticated
- 400 Bad Request with validation errors for:
  - Missing/empty title (TODO_TITLE_REQUIRED)
  - Title > 200 chars (TODO_TITLE_TOO_LONG)
  - Description > 5000 chars (TODO_DESCRIPTION_TOO_LONG)
  - Invalid date format (TODO_INVALID_DATE)

responseBody.description: The newly created todo with all fields including generated id and timestamps

requestBody.description: Todo creation data with required title and optional description, start_date, and due_date

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of todos belonging to the authenticated user.

This operation provides comprehensive todo list viewing capabilities with multiple organization options. Users can filter todos by completion status to view all todos, only completed todos, or only incomplete todos. Multiple sorting options are available including by creation date (newest or oldest first), start date (earliest or latest first), and due date (earliest or latest first).

When sorting by start_date or due_date, todos without those dates set appear at the end of the results, ensuring consistent ordering behavior. Only active (non-deleted) todos are shown in this list; deleted todos in the trash are accessed through separate trash endpoints.

Each todo in the response includes the title, completion status, start_date if set, due_date if set, and creation date. The full description is not included in list items to optimize response size; use the individual todo endpoint to retrieve complete details.

Privacy is strictly enforced: users can only view their own todos, and all queries are automatically scoped to the authenticated user's data.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implementation requires querying the todo_app_todos table with the following constraints:

1. Always filter by user_id matching the authenticated user's ID
2. Always filter is_deleted = false to exclude trashed todos
3. Apply completion status filter based on request: is_completed = true for 'complete', is_completed = false for 'incomplete', no filter for 'all'
4. Apply sorting based on request parameter: created_at, start_date, or due_date with ASC or DESC direction
5. For start_date and due_date sorting, use NULLS LAST to place todos without dates at the end
6. Implement cursor-based or offset-based pagination with configurable page size
7. Return todos with id, title, is_completed, start_date, due_date, created_at fields

Database indexes available for optimization: (user_id, is_deleted, created_at), (user_id, is_deleted, start_date), (user_id, is_deleted, due_date). Select appropriate index based on sort field.

Edge cases: Empty result set returns empty data array with pagination showing zero total. Invalid filter values default to 'all'. Invalid sort field defaults to created_at descending.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of todo summaries matching the search criteria

requestBody.description: Search criteria including completion status filter, sorting options, and pagination parameters

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information for a specific todo item.

This operation fetches a single todo by its unique identifier, returning all fields including the full description. The operation enforces strict data privacy: users can only access their own todos, and attempting to access another user's todo will result in a not found error without revealing the todo's existence.

The todo must be active (is_deleted = false) to be retrieved. If the todo has been soft-deleted and moved to trash, this operation returns a not found error. Users should use the trash endpoints to access deleted todos.

The response includes all todo fields: the unique identifier, title (required), description (may be null), optional start and due dates, completion status, and timestamps for creation and last modification.
operations.name: at

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the todo to retrieve
parameters.name: todoId

responseBody.description: Complete todo details including all fields

operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. Validate the todoId parameter is a valid UUID
2. Query the todo_app_todos table for a record matching the provided id
3. Verify the todo exists and belongs to the authenticated user (user_id matches current user)
4. Verify the todo is not soft-deleted (is_deleted = false)
5. If todo not found, belongs to another user, or is deleted, return 404 NOT_FOUND error with code TODO_NOT_FOUND
6. Return the complete todo entity with all fields

Database query:
- SELECT * FROM todo_app_todos WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ? AND is_deleted = false

Security considerations:
- Use the same error response for non-existent todos and todos belonging to other users to prevent information leakage
- Do not reveal whether a todo ID exists but belongs to another user

prerequisites.description: A todo must be created before it can be retrieved by its ID. This prerequisite establishes the todo resource with the authenticated user as its owner, generating the todoId needed for the GET operation.

operations.description:
Update an existing todo's title, description, start date, or due date.

This operation allows authenticated users to modify the content of their active todos. Only the following fields can be updated: title (required, max 200 characters), description (optional, max 5000 characters), start_date (optional), and due_date (optional). Fields not included in the request body remain unchanged.

Every successful edit automatically creates a history entry in the todo_app_todo_histories table, recording the timestamp and the new values of all modified fields. This provides a complete audit trail of all changes made to each todo.

The operation enforces strict privacy controls: users can only update todos they own. Attempting to update another user's todo returns a not found error without revealing the todo's existence. Todos that have been soft-deleted (moved to trash) cannot be edited and will return an error.

Validation rules:
- Title must be non-empty after trimming whitespace
- Title maximum length is 200 characters
- Description maximum length is 5000 characters
- Dates must be valid ISO 8601 format if provided
- At least one field must be different from current values to create a history entry

Related operations:
- PATCH /todos/{todoId}/complete - Mark todo as complete
- PATCH /todos/{todoId}/incomplete - Mark todo as incomplete
- GET /todos/{todoId}/history - View edit history for this todo
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. Extract todoId from path parameter and validate it's a valid UUID

2. Authenticate the user from the request context

3. Query todo_app_todos table to find the todo:
   - WHERE id = todoId AND user_id = authenticated_user_id AND is_deleted = false
   - If not found, return 404 NOT_FOUND error (do not reveal whether todo exists for another user)

4. Validate request body fields:
   - Title: required, trim whitespace, reject if empty, max 200 characters
   - Description: optional, max 5000 characters if provided
   - start_date: optional, validate ISO 8601 format if provided
   - due_date: optional, validate ISO 8601 format if provided

5. Compare request values to current todo values:
   - Only include fields that have actually changed in the update
   - If no fields changed, return success without creating history entry

6. Execute database transaction:
   a. Update todo_app_todos record:
      - SET modified fields to new values
      - SET updated_at = current_timestamp
   b. Create history entry in todo_app_todo_histories:
      - Record timestamp
      - Store new values for each modified field (title, description, start_date, due_date)
      - Omit fields that were not changed

7. Return the updated ITodoAppTodo entity

Error handling:
- 404 NOT_FOUND: Todo doesn't exist, belongs to another user, or is deleted
- 400 BAD_REQUEST: Validation errors (empty title, title too long, description too long, invalid date format)
- 401 UNAUTHORIZED: User not authenticated

responseBody.description: The updated todo entity with all current field values

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo to update. Must be a valid UUID. The todo must exist, belong to the authenticated user, and not be in the trash.
parameters.name: todoId

requestBody.description: Todo update data containing only editable fields. Title is required and will be trimmed. Description and dates are optional. Omitted fields remain unchanged.

prerequisites.description: Todo must be created before it can be updated. This operation creates the todo entity that the update operation modifies.

operations.description:
Set the completion status of a todo to complete.

This operation sets the is_completed field of a todo to true. The todo must belong to the authenticated user and must not be in the trash (is_deleted must be false). The updated_at timestamp is automatically updated when the completion status changes.

Unlike todo editing operations that modify title, description, or dates, marking a todo complete does not create an entry in the edit history. The completion status is a binary state (true/false) that can be toggled independently of the content edit tracking system.

The operation requires authentication and enforces complete data isolation - users can only complete their own todos. Attempting to complete a todo belonging to another user, a deleted todo, or a non-existent todo will result in an appropriate error response.
operations.name: complete
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. Validate the todoId path parameter as a valid UUID
2. Query todo_app_todos table for the specified todo where:
   - id = todoId
   - user_id = authenticated user's ID (from JWT token)
   - is_deleted = false
3. If no todo found, return 404 Not Found
4. Update the todo record:
   - Set is_completed = true
   - Set updated_at = current timestamp
5. Return the updated todo entity with all fields

Note: Do NOT create a history entry in todo_app_todo_histories - completion status changes are explicitly excluded from history tracking per business requirements.

responseBody.description: The updated todo entity with completion status set to true

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo to mark as complete
parameters.name: todoId

prerequisites.description: A todo must exist before it can be marked as complete. This operation creates the todo entity that will be referenced by the todoId path parameter in the complete operation.

operations.description:
Mark a specific todo as incomplete.

This operation sets the completion status of a todo to incomplete (is_completed = false). It is designed for users who want to mark a previously completed todo as incomplete, effectively reverting it to an unfinished state.

The operation validates that the target todo exists, belongs to the authenticated user, and is not currently in the trash (soft-deleted). If any of these conditions are not met, the operation returns a not found error without revealing whether the todo belongs to another user, maintaining strict privacy between users.

Unlike todo editing operations, completion status changes do NOT create edit history entries. This allows users to freely toggle completion status without cluttering their todo history with completion state changes.

The operation is idempotent - if the todo is already marked as incomplete, the operation succeeds without error and returns the todo unchanged.

Upon successful completion, the updated_at timestamp is refreshed to reflect the modification time, and the complete todo entity is returned to the caller.
operations.name: incomplete
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. Extract todoId from path parameters and validate it is a valid UUID format.

2. Query the todo_app_todos table for a record matching:
   - id = todoId
   - user_id = authenticated user's ID
   - is_deleted = false

3. If no record is found, return a 404 NOT_FOUND error with code TODO_NOT_FOUND. Do not reveal whether the todo exists but belongs to another user or is deleted.

4. If the todo's is_completed is already false, return the existing todo without modification (idempotent behavior).

5. Update the todo record:
   - Set is_completed = false
   - Set updated_at = current timestamp

6. Do NOT create a todo_app_todo_histories entry - completion status changes are excluded from history tracking.

7. Return the updated todo entity with all fields populated.

responseBody.description: The updated todo entity with is_completed set to false

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo to mark as incomplete
parameters.name: todoId

prerequisites.description: Todo must exist before it can be marked as incomplete. This prerequisite creates the todo entity that will be referenced by the todoId path parameter.

operations.description:
Removes a todo from the active list by moving it to the trash.

This operation performs a soft delete on the specified todo, setting the is_deleted flag to true without removing the data from storage. The todo will no longer appear in normal todo list queries but remains accessible through the trash endpoint for potential restoration.

The operation verifies that the authenticated user owns the todo before performing the deletion. If the todo belongs to another user or does not exist, the system returns a not found error without revealing the existence of other users' data.

All todo data is preserved during this operation, including the title, description, dates, completion status, and the complete edit history stored in todo_app_todo_histories. The updated_at timestamp is set to the current time to reflect when the deletion occurred.

After deletion, the todo can be viewed in the trash list (GET /trash), restored to the active list (POST /trash/{todoId}/restore), or permanently deleted (DELETE /trash/{todoId}) which removes both the todo and its edit history.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. Validate the todoId path parameter is a valid UUID format
2. Query todo_app_todos table for the todo with matching id
3. Verify the todo exists and belongs to the authenticated user (user_id matches)
4. Verify the todo is not already soft-deleted (is_deleted = false)
5. If todo not found, belongs to another user, or already deleted: return 404 Not Found
6. Update the todo record:
   - SET is_deleted = true
   - SET updated_at = current timestamp
7. Return the updated todo entity

Database query:
```sql
UPDATE todo_app_todos 
SET is_deleted = true, updated_at = NOW() 
WHERE id = $1 AND user_id = $2 AND is_deleted = false
RETURNING *
```

Privacy enforcement: The user_id condition in the WHERE clause ensures users can only delete their own todos. The same 404 response is returned whether the todo doesn't exist, belongs to another user, or is already deleted, preventing information leakage.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo to delete (UUID format)
parameters.name: todoId

prerequisites.description: A todo must exist before it can be soft-deleted. POST /todoApp/user/todos creates a new todo owned by the authenticated user, which can then be referenced by todoId and moved to trash.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of edit history entries for a specific todo.

This operation provides users with a comprehensive audit trail of all modifications made to their todo item. Each history entry captures when an edit occurred and which fields were changed during that edit operation.

**Access Control**: Users can only view history for their own todos. Attempting to access history for another user's todo will result in an authorization error. This enforces complete data privacy between users.

**History Entry Content**: Each entry includes the timestamp (created_at) of when the edit was made. Fields that were modified contain their new values; fields that were not modified during that edit are null. For example, if only the title was changed, only the title field will have a value while description, start_date, and due_date will be null.

**Sorting**: History entries are returned sorted from most recent to oldest (descending by created_at timestamp), allowing users to see the most recent changes first.

**Availability**: Edit history is available for active todos, trashed todos, and restored todos. When a todo is permanently deleted from trash, all associated history entries are cascade deleted.

**Related Operations**: To view the current state of the todo, use GET /todos/{todoId}. To restore a deleted todo, use POST /trash/{todoId}/restore.
operations.name: index

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the todo whose edit history is being retrieved. The user must own this todo to access its history.
parameters.name: todoId

requestBody.description: Pagination parameters for the history list. Supports standard pagination with limit and cursor-based navigation.

operations.specification:
Implementation guidance for the todo history index operation:

1. **Authorization Check**: Verify the authenticated user owns the todo by querying todo_app_todos where id = {todoId} AND user_id = current_user.id. Include is_deleted = false for active todos or allow viewing history for trashed todos as well (requirements state history should be accessible for trashed todos).

2. **Query Execution**: 
   - Query todo_app_todo_histories table where todo_app_todo_id = {todoId}
   - Sort by created_at DESC (most recent first)
   - Apply pagination using the standard cursor-based pattern
   - Use the existing index on [todo_app_todo_id, created_at] for optimal performance

3. **Response Construction**:
   - For each history entry, include:
     - id (UUID)
     - created_at (DateTime - the edit timestamp)
     - title (String? - null means not changed)
     - description (String? - null means not changed)
     - start_date (DateTime? - null means not changed)
     - due_date (DateTime? - null means not changed)
   - Wrap in pagination structure with next_cursor

4. **Edge Cases**:
   - If todo doesn't exist: return 404 Not Found
   - If user doesn't own the todo: return 403 Forbidden
   - If no history entries exist: return empty data array (valid response)

5. **Performance Considerations**:
   - Use the compound index [todo_app_todo_id, created_at] for efficient querying
   - Limit default page size to prevent large responses
   - Response time target: under 2 seconds for todos with up to 100 history entries

prerequisites.description: Todo must exist before its edit history can be retrieved. The todoId path parameter references a todo entity that must be created first and owned by the authenticated user.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of soft-deleted todos from the authenticated user's trash.

This endpoint displays todos that have been moved to trash through the soft delete mechanism. Each todo in the trash has its is_deleted flag set to true in the todo_app_todos table. Users can only view their own trashed todos - complete data isolation is enforced at the database query level through the user_id foreign key relationship.

The trash list supports pagination with configurable page sizes (10-50 items, default 20) to handle users with large numbers of deleted todos efficiently. Results are sorted by modification date in descending order, showing most recently deleted todos first. The updated_at field captures when the is_deleted flag was changed, serving as an effective deletion timestamp. Each todo entry displays summary information: title, completion status, start date (if set), due date (if set), and creation date.

This endpoint does not display todos that are currently active (is_deleted=false). To view active todos, use the main todo list endpoint. Trashed todos can be restored using POST /trash/{id}/restore or permanently deleted using DELETE /trash/{id}. Permanent deletion removes the todo and all associated edit history entries irreversibly.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query todo_app_todos table WHERE user_id = authenticated_user.id AND is_deleted = true. Apply pagination using LIMIT and OFFSET based on page and pageSize parameters from request body. Sort by created_at in descending order by default, or according to sortBy and sortOrder parameters if provided. Select only summary fields: id, title, is_completed, start_date, due_date, created_at. Exclude description field for performance optimization. Return total count of trashed todos for pagination metadata. Implement efficient database indexing on (user_id, is_deleted, created_at) for fast queries.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of trashed todos with summary information

requestBody.description: Pagination and sorting parameters for trash list

operations.description:
Restore a previously deleted todo from the trash back to the active todo list.

This operation reverses the soft delete action by setting the is_deleted flag to false, making the todo visible again in the normal todo list. The todo retains all its original data including title, description, dates, and completion status.

The authenticated user can only restore their own todos. Attempting to restore a todo belonging to another user will result in a 404 Not Found error, maintaining complete privacy between users.

If the todo is not currently in the trash (is_deleted = false), the operation will return a 400 Bad Request error as the todo is already active. If the todo does not exist, a 404 Not Found error is returned.

After restoration, the todo will appear in normal todo list queries and can be edited, completed, or deleted again.
operations.name: restore
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. Extract authenticated user ID from the request context
2. Validate todoId parameter is a valid UUID format
3. Query todo_app_todos table for a record matching:
   - id = todoId (path parameter)
   - user_id = authenticated user ID (ensures privacy)
   - is_deleted = true (must be in trash to restore)
4. If no record found:
   - If todo exists but belongs to different user: return 404 Not Found
   - If todo exists but is_deleted = false: return 400 Bad Request (already active)
   - If todo doesn't exist: return 404 Not Found
5. Update the todo record:
   - Set is_deleted = false
   - Set updated_at = current timestamp
6. Return the complete updated todo entity

Database query:
```sql
UPDATE todo_app_todos
SET is_deleted = false, updated_at = NOW()
WHERE id = $todoId AND user_id = $userId AND is_deleted = true
RETURNING *
```

Authorization: Requires authenticated user (member role). Only the todo owner can restore.

responseBody.description: The restored todo with all its details

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo to restore from trash

prerequisites.description: Todo must be created before it can be restored from the trash

operations.description:
Permanently delete a todo from the trash.

This operation irreversibly removes a todo that has been soft-deleted (moved to trash). The todo and all its associated edit history entries from todo_app_todo_histories are permanently deleted from the database. This action cannot be undone.

The operation enforces strict privacy controls: users can only permanently delete their own todos. The target todo must already be in the trash (is_deleted=true); attempting to permanently delete an active todo will result in an error.

Before permanent deletion, users should consider using the restore endpoint (POST /trash/{todoId}/restore) if they want to recover the todo. Once permanently deleted, there is no way to recover the todo or its history.

Related operations:
- DELETE /todos/{todoId} - Soft delete todo (move to trash)
- POST /trash/{todoId}/restore - Restore deleted todo from trash
- GET /trash - List deleted todos in trash
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Permanently delete a todo from the trash.

Implementation steps:
1. Extract todoId from path parameter
2. Query todo_app_todos table with conditions:
   - id = todoId
   - user_id = authenticated user's ID
   - is_deleted = true (must be in trash)
3. If no record found, return 404 Not Found (todo doesn't exist, not owned by user, or not in trash)
4. Execute DELETE on todo_app_todos
5. Cascade delete automatically removes all related todo_app_todo_histories entries via onDelete: Cascade constraint
6. Return success response

Edge cases:
- Todo not found: Return 404
- Todo not in trash (is_deleted=false): Return 404 (user should use soft delete first)
- Todo owned by different user: Return 404 (privacy - don't reveal existence)

Database transaction:
- Single DELETE query with WHERE clause including user_id and is_deleted conditions
- Prisma handles cascade delete of histories automatically via schema relation

current.description:

Indicates which page of results is currently being returned. Page
numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1 (not 0). This value
reflects the page parameter from the request after validation and bounds
checking.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records per page.

Defines the upper bound on how many records can be returned in a single
page. This corresponds to the limit parameter from the request. The
actual number of records in the data array may be less than this value on
the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum records per page. Actual count may be less on last page.

records.description:
Total count of all records matching the query criteria.

Represents the complete number of records available across all pages, not
just the current page. This value is computed via a COUNT query and is

elements like "Showing 1-10 of 150 results".
records.x-autobe-specification: Total record count across all pages.

pages.description:
Total number of pages available.

Calculated as ceiling of {@link records} divided by {@link limit}. When
records is 0, pages will also be 0. This value enables clients to render
page navigation controls and validate page bounds.

This interface provides comprehensive pagination information returned

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.
refreshable_until.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token expiration timestamp. Re-authentication required after this time.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
JWT-based authorization token pair with expiration metadata.

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.
IAuthorizationToken.x-autobe-specification: Dual-token authentication structure with access/refresh tokens and expiration info.

ITodoAppUser.IAuthorized.description: Authentication response containing the authenticated user's identifier, display name, and JWT token pair for API access. Returned by join, login, and refresh endpoints to provide clients with all credentials needed for authenticated API calls. The access token should be included in the Authorization header (Bearer scheme) for protected endpoints. The refresh token enables session continuation without re-authentication.
ITodoAppUser.IAuthorized.x-autobe-specification: Computed authentication response type. Implementation: 1) Extract user id from authenticated user context or JWT sub claim. 2) Query todo_app_users table to retrieve display_name where id = user_id. 3) Generate JWT access token (15 min expiration) with claims: sub (user id), iat (issued at timestamp), exp (expiration), role ('user'), jti (unique token id). 4) Generate JWT refresh token (30 days expiration) with claims: sub, iat, exp, type ('refresh'), jti. 5) Compute expired_at as current time + 15 minutes. 6) Compute refreshable_until as current time + 30 days. 7) Return object with id, display_name, and nested token object containing access, refresh, expired_at, refreshable_until. ITodoAppTodo.description: Complete todo entity representing a user's personal task. Includes unique identifier, title, optional description, optional start and due dates, completion status, soft delete flag, owner information, and timestamps. Each todo is strictly scoped to its owning user, ensuring complete data isolation between users.
ITodoAppTodo.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from todo_app_todos table with FK-to-object transformation. Column mappings: id (primary key UUID), title, description (nullable), start_date → startDate (nullable), due_date → dueDate (nullable), is_completed → isCompleted, is_deleted → isDeleted, created_at → createdAt, updated_at → updatedAt. The user_id foreign key column is transformed to the 'user' belongs-to relation, exposing the owner as ITodoAppUser.ISummary. Nullable fields use oneOf with null type. The histories has-many relation is excluded (accessible via dedicated history endpoints).
